proposals.before: In spring, the first month, Wang Jingze was made Grand Cavalry General and Minister of Works; Chen Xianda was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Jiang Province.
proposals.after: In spring, the first month, Grand Cavalry General Wang Jingze was made Minister of Works; General Who Pacifies the Army Chen Xianda was made Governor of Jiang Province.
proposals.reason: The Chinese appoints already-titled officers to new posts (以A為B); the literal English wrongly treats 驃騎大將軍 and 鎮軍大將軍 as the offices being conferred.

proposals.before: When the emperor heard of it, he appointed Cui Huijing Right Guards General and Governor of Yu Province to guard against it.
proposals.after: When the emperor heard of it, he appointed Right Guards General Cui Huijing Governor of Yu Province to guard against it.
proposals.reason: 以右衛將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史 makes him Yu governor while he already holds Right Guards General; the literal invents a dual appointment.

proposals.before: Xing Luan was a grandson of Xing Shuo.
proposals.after: Xing Luan was a grandson of Xing Ying.
proposals.reason: 穎 is Ying, not Shuo; the English personal name does not match the Chinese given name.

proposals.before: Luan was the grandson of Xing Shuo.
proposals.after: Luan was the grandson of Xing Ying.
proposals.reason: Same mismatch of 穎 with the spelling Shuo.

proposals.before: On bingzi, Crown Prince Wenhuiz Changmao died.
proposals.after: On bingzi, Crown Prince Wenhui Changmao died.
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui; Wenhuiz is a corrupted romanization.

proposals.before: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince Zhaoye of Nan Commandery was named imperial great-grandson; Eastern Palace officials were retitled as great-grandson staff; the late crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, became great-grandson grand consort; and Prince Zhaoye's consort, Lady He, became great-grandson consort.
proposals.after: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince Zhaoye of Nan Commandery was named imperial grandson; Eastern Palace officials were retitled as imperial-grandson staff; the late crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, became grand consort to the imperial grandson; and Prince Zhaoye's consort, Lady He, became consort of the imperial grandson.
proposals.reason: 皇太孫 is the emperor's grandson (the crown prince's son), not a great-grandson.

proposals.before: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince of Nanjun Zhaoye was established as imperial great-grandson; all Eastern Palace civil and military offices were changed to great-grandson staff; the crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, was made great-grandson grand consort; the Prince of Nanjun's consort, Lady He, was made great-grandson consort.
proposals.after: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince of Nanjun Zhaoye was established as imperial grandson; all Eastern Palace civil and military offices were changed to imperial-grandson staff; the crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, was made grand consort to the imperial grandson; the Prince of Nanjun's consort, Lady He, was made consort of the imperial grandson.
proposals.reason: Same 太孫 versus great-grandson error in the literal English.

proposals.before: Lady He was a daughter of the Ji clan.
proposals.after: Lady He was a daughter of Ji.
proposals.reason: 戢 is the father's given name, not a clan name.

proposals.before: In the past Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao with ten thousand exhausted troops, and Xie Xuan crushed Fu Qin's army with three thousand infantry—the outcome turns in a moment, not on numbers alone."
proposals.after: In the past Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao with ten thousand exhausted troops, and Xie Xuan crushed the army of Former Qin with three thousand infantry—the outcome turns in a moment, not on numbers alone."
proposals.reason: 苻秦 names the Former Qin state, not a person Fu Qin; the idiomatic English treats it as a personal name.

proposals.before: On the day dingwei the Wei emperor held a military review and put Minister of Works Li Chong in charge of selecting troops.
proposals.after: On the day dingwei the Wei emperor held a military review and put Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong in charge of selecting troops.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尚書李沖 is the Masters of Writing, not 司空 (Minister of Works), which this chapter already assigned to Mu Liang.

proposals.before: On dingwei the Wei sovereign held a military review and ordered Minister of Works Li Chong to oversee selection for martial service.
proposals.after: On dingwei the Wei sovereign held a military review and ordered Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong to oversee selection for martial service.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 尚書 as Minister of Works, colliding with 司空 in s0073.

proposals.before: Governor Wang Xuanyao put down the revolt and executed the ringleaders.
proposals.after: Governor Wang Xuanmiao put down the revolt and executed the ringleaders.
proposals.reason: 玄邈 is Xuanmiao; Xuanyao is a wrong pinyin reading of 邈.

proposals.before: Governor Wang Xuanyao suppressed and executed them.
proposals.after: Governor Wang Xuanmiao suppressed and executed them.
proposals.reason: The literal field repeats the same wrong reading of 邈 as yao rather than miao.

proposals.before: Before long the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guard, weapons and all, and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.
proposals.after: Before long the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guard, weapons and all, and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.
proposals.reason: 尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, not Vice Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: Shortly after, the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guards with their weapons inside and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.
proposals.after: Shortly after, the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guards with their weapons inside and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.
proposals.reason: 尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, not Vice Minister of Works.

proposals.before: Rong saw that his plan had failed, changed out of mourning dress, returned to the Secretariat, and sighed, "My lord, you have led me astray!"
proposals.after: Rong saw that his plan had failed, changed out of martial dress, returned to the Secretariat, and sighed, "My lord, you have led me astray!"
proposals.reason: 釋服 follows 戎服絳衫 in s0150; he discarded battle dress, not the mourning clothes of s0143.

proposals.before: Rong knew his plan had failed; he changed back from mourning dress and returned to the Secretariat, sighing: "My lord—you have ruined me!"
proposals.after: Rong knew his plan had failed; he changed back from martial dress and returned to the Secretariat, sighing: "My lord—you have ruined me!"
proposals.reason: 釋服 refers to removing the martial scarlet shirt, not mourning dress.

proposals.before: Prince of Wuling Ye declared loudly before the assembly: "If a commoner is to be enthroned, it ought to be me;
proposals.after: Prince of Wuling Ye declared loudly before the assembly: "If a lesser prince is to be enthroned, it ought to be me;
proposals.reason: 立民 contrasts with 立嫡 and means a cadet or lesser prince, not a commoner; the idiomatic rendering is correct.

proposals.before: Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis Luan of Xichang, was made Director of the Secretariat;
proposals.after: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis Luan of Xichang, was made Director of the Secretariat;
proposals.reason: 尚書左僕射 is not Vice Minister of Works.

proposals.before: Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis of Xichang Luan, became Director of the Secretariat;
proposals.after: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis of Xichang Luan, became Director of the Secretariat;
proposals.reason: 尚書左僕射 is not Vice Minister of Works.

proposals.before: In Wei, Wei Yuan, Marquis Jingzhuang of Shanyang, died.
proposals.after: In Wei, Yu Yuan, Marquis Jinghuan of Shanyang, died.
proposals.reason: The surname is 尉 (Yu), not Wei; the posthumous name is 景桓 (Jinghuan), not Jingzhuang.

proposals.before: In Wei, Marquis Jingzhuang of Shanyang, Wei Yuan, died.
proposals.after: In Wei, Marquis Jinghuan of Shanyang, Yu Yuan, died.
proposals.reason: 尉元 is Yu Yuan and 景桓 is Jinghuan; Zhuang and the surname Wei are mistranslations.

proposals.before: He then appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and commander of all forces west of the Pass, with Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Xue Yin all serving as Gan's deputies; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.
proposals.after: He then appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and commander of all forces west of the Pass, with Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Calms the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Xue Yin all serving as Gan's deputies; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.
proposals.reason: 安南將軍 and 平南將軍 are distinct titles; the idiomatic English renders both as General Who Pacifies the South.

proposals.before: He appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs west of the Pass, and further made Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Ping Xue Yin all deputies to Gan; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.
proposals.after: He appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs west of the Pass, and further made Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Calms the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Xue Yin all deputies to Gan; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.
proposals.reason: Literal English fuses 平南 with the surname as Ping Xue Yin; 薛胤 is Xue Yin, and 安南/平南 should remain distinct.

proposals.before: Yet he affectingly feigned emotion and practiced deception, secretly harboring base malice; he shared food and clothing with his favored low companions and slept and rose with them.
proposals.after: Yet he feigned emotion and practiced deception, secretly harboring base malice; he shared food and clothing with his favored low companions and slept and rose with them.
proposals.reason: Affectingly is ungrammatical and obscures 矯情飾詐.

proposals.before: Masters Shi Renzu and Hu Tianyi, attendants in the secretariat, said to each other, "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;
proposals.after: His tutor Shi Renzu and the attendant-scribe Hu Tianyi said to each other, "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;
proposals.reason: 師 is the office of tutor before 史仁祖; 侍書 is Hu Tianyi's office, not a shared secretariat mastership.

proposals.before: Masters Shi Renzu and Hu Tianyi, attendants in the secretariat, said to each other: "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;
proposals.after: Tutor Shi Renzu and attendant-scribe Hu Tianyi said to each other: "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;
proposals.reason: Same office split: 師史仁祖、侍書胡天翼 should not be collapsed into Masters ... attendants in the secretariat.

proposals.before: Then he said to Grand Secretary Feng Yan, "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."
proposals.after: Then he said to Minister of Education Feng Yan, "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education / Director of Instruction, not Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: Then he said to Grand Secretary Feng Yan: "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."
proposals.after: Then he said to Minister of Education Feng Yan: "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."
proposals.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 司徒 as Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: On the day yihai King Su Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;
proposals.after: On the day yihai King Xiangshu Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;
proposals.reason: 像舒 is the Dengzhi king's two-character surname and 彭 the given name; 'Su Peng' misreads 像舒彭.

proposals.before: On yihai King Su Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;
proposals.after: On yihai King Xiangshu Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 像舒彭 as 'Su Peng' in the literal English.

proposals.before: I have long dwelt in the northern wilds and wish to move south to the central lands;
proposals.after: My house has for generations dwelt in the northern wilds, and I wish to move south to the central lands;
proposals.reason: 世居 means hereditary or generational residence, not merely a long personal sojourn.

proposals.before: Yin Zhibo sent the army commander Xie Deren and others to lead several thousand troops to join and support them.
proposals.after: Yin Zhibo sent the army commander Xi Deren and others to lead several thousand troops to join and support them.
proposals.reason: The surname 席 is Xi, not Xie.

proposals.before: Yin Zhibo sent the army commander Xie Deren and others to lead several thousand troops to join and support them.
proposals.after: Yin Zhibo sent the army commander Xi Deren and others to lead several thousand troops to join and support them.
proposals.reason: Same surname error 席 rendered as Xie in the literal English.

decisions.reason: 以驃騎大將軍王敬則為司空 names an already titled officer and confers 司空; the original treats 驃騎大將軍 as newly given.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以驃騎大將軍王敬則為司空

decisions.reason: 以右衛將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史 confers 豫州刺史 on a man already titled 右衛將軍; the original invents a dual appointment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以右衛將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史

decisions.reason: 穎 is Ying; Shuo would be 朔, so Xing Shuo is a wrong given-name reading.
The literal likewise renders 穎 as Shuo; Xing Ying matches the graph and pinyin Yǐng.
文惠 is Wenhui; Wenhuiz is a stray letter not present in the Chinese title.
皇太孫 is the emperor's grandson, the late crown prince's son, not a great-grandson.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 立南郡王昭業為皇太孫

decisions.reason: 太孫官屬 and 皇太孫妃 likewise belong to the imperial grandson, not a great-grandson.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 東宮文武悉改為太孫官屬

decisions.reason: Parallel 後，熙之女也 shows 戢 is the father's given name, not a clan name Ji.
苻秦 is the Former Qin state; the next sentence's 苻氏 confirms a polity, not a person Fu Qin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 謝玄以步兵三千摧苻秦

decisions.reason: 尚書李沖 is a Master of Writing, not 司空; Minister of Works would be a different office.
The literal repeats the same 尚書-as-司空 error for 李沖.
邈 is miǎo; Xuanyao misreads 王玄邈 as if 邈 were yào.
The literal has the same wrong reading of 邈; Xuanmiao is the correct romanization.
尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Vice Minister of Works (司空).
The literal likewise misidentifies 尚書左僕射 as a Works ministry post.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以朝事委尚書左僕射西昌侯鸞

decisions.reason: s0150 has 戎服絳衫; 釋服 is discarding that martial dress, not mourning clothes.
The literal's mourning dress contradicts the scarlet battle shirt Wang Rong was wearing.
立民 is opposed to 立嫡 and means a cadet or lesser prince; Ye is not calling himself a commoner.
尚書左僕射 again is the secretariat vice-directorate, not Minister of Works.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書左僕射、西昌侯鸞為尚書令

decisions.reason: The literal repeats the 僕射/司空 confusion at Luan's promotion to 尚書令.
尉 is the surname Yu, not Wei; 景桓 is Jinghuan, not Jingzhuang.
The literal has the same surname and posthumous-name errors for 尉元 and 景桓.
安南將軍 and 平南將軍 are distinct titles; rendering both as Pacifies the South collapses them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安南將軍盧淵、平南將軍薛胤

decisions.reason: 平南將軍薛胤 is Xue Yin; Ping Xue Yin fuses the title 平南 with the surname.
Affectingly is ungrammatical; 矯情飾詐 is feigning feeling and dressing up deceit.
師史仁祖 and 侍書胡天翼 are two offices: tutor and attendant-scribe, not joint secretariat masters.
The literal likewise merges 師 and 侍書 into one invented secretariat mastership.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 師史仁祖、侍書胡天翼相謂曰

decisions.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education, not Grand Secretary.
The literal repeats the 司徒-as-Grand-Secretary error for 馮誕.
像舒彭 is Xiangshu Peng; Su Peng drops 像 and misreads the two-character surname.
The literal has the same misreading of 像舒彭 as Su Peng.
世居 marks generational residence in 幽朔, not merely that the speaker has long dwelt there.
席德仁 is Xi Deren; Xie would be 謝, not 席.
The literal repeats the 席-as-Xie surname error.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0026 shows 師 belongs only to Shi Renzu; the attendant role was created by collapsing him with 侍書胡天翼.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 restores 穎 as Ying; Shuo is not a reading of that graph.
Accepted r0003 corrects the inferred personal name to Xing Ying to match 邢穎.
Accepted r0012 restores 邈 as miao; Xuanyao was created by the bad romanization.
Accepted r0021 restores the surname 尉 as Yu; Wei would be 魏.
Accepted r0021 restores 桓 as Huan; Zhuang would be 莊.
Accepted r0023 distinguishes 安南將軍 from 平南將軍; Pacifies the South belonged only to the latter in the repaired English.
Accepted r0030 restores 像舒彭 as Xiangshu Peng; Su Peng was created by dropping 像.
Accepted r0033 restores 席 as Xi; Xie Deren was created by reading 席 as 謝.
